div.head: ECf 32 A
div.ab: Et similiter olim apud Britones, temporibus Romanorum, in regno isto Britannie uocabantur senatores qui postea temporibus Saxonum, ut predictum est, uocabantur aldermanni, non propter etatem sed propter sapientiam et dignitatem, cum quidem adolescentes essent, iuris periti et super hoc experti et, ut uerum fatear, non ignari.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 655 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page as an insertion into ECf retr. 32 (32 A–E, pp. 655–660). The dictionary cites it as “ECf 32 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.

The words in smaller type in Liebermann’s print (uocabantur aldermanni, non propter, sed propter sapientiam, cum quidem adolescentes essent) are taken over from ECf retr. 32, 3 (marked with a dagger); his margin gives the source.

note.seg: cf. Wl art. retr., Inscr., note d
er betont auch sonst die Alderman-Würde, die schon Will. fil. Stephani senatoriam dignitatem nennt (bes. das Wardimot o. S. 525b); vgl. über aldermen um 1200 Bateson Engl. hist. rev. 1902, 507

he stresses the dignity of alderman elsewhere too, which William fitz Stephen already calls senatoriam dignitatem (esp. the Wardimot, above p. 525, note b); on aldermen around 1200 cf. Bateson, Engl. hist. rev. 1902, 507
Et neuer Satz ohne n. i. Ld
Et a new sentence, without n. i. Ld

div.ab: And likewise formerly among the Britons, in the times of the Romans, in this kingdom of Britain, those were called senators who afterwards in the times of the Saxons, as was said before, were called aldermen, not on account of age but on account of wisdom and dignity, although indeed they were young men, skilled in the law and experienced in it and, to confess the truth, not ignorant.
